value: no fovea reported; ganglion cell layer cells peak in the temporal retina of adults (higher acuity in the frontal field); in juveniles the peak is in the ventral retina (better acuity in the upper field)
method: whole-mounted retinas, density and distribution of photoreceptors and ganglion cell layer cells (abstract)
conditions: adult and juvenile B. jararaca compared; rattlesnake Crotalus durissus also studied

source.authors: Tashiro JH, Ventura DF, Hauzman E
source.title: Morphological plasticity of the retina of Viperidae snakes is associated with ontogenetic changes in ecology and behavior

where: Abstract; two consecutive pieces joined at 'B. jararaca,' / 'indicating'
quote: The GCL cells had peak densities in the temporal retina of C. durissus and adults of B. jararaca, indicating higher acuity in the frontal field.
note: Abstract level via a DOAJ-style mirror; the trait key fovea is used for the position of the area of peak ganglion-cell density, no number given. Crotalus durissus shares the temporal peak.

value: full-length RH1 and LWS opsin genes and most of SWS1 cloned, so at least three opsin classes; potential for rudimentary colour vision in a nocturnal viper
method: opsin gene cloning and sequencing from the retina (abstract); opsin-inferred, no microspectrophotometry

source.title: Opsin-based photopigments expressed in the retina of a South American pit viper, Bothrops atrox (Viperidae)

where: Abstract; two consecutive pieces joined at 'viper,' / 'specifically'
quote: This is the first report to support the potential for rudimentary color vision in a South American viper, specifically a species that is regarded as being nocturnal.
note: Abstract level via a repository page; the abstract states no lambda max values. Opsin-inferred, so grade g at most. Author list on the page was Katti, Christiana only.

method: chemical analysis and bioassay of floral scent (abstract)

quote: We further demonstrate that C. crebra attracts its single pollinator species with a unique system of (methylthio)phenols, three of which are new natural products.
